PUBLIC COMMENT
Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter
not on the agenda may do so at this time. State law (Government Code Section 54950 et seq.) prohibits the City
Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .
Upon request, the City Council may, in their discretion, allow citizen participation on a specific item on the agenda
at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person
shall make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting
a meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the
individual’s failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Argumedo called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Library Director Bautista led the Pledge of Allegiance.

INVOCATION Councilmember Lainez offered the invocation.

PUBLIC COMMENT Honey Bizarro, Jasmine Gonzalez and Aida Vega spoke about the need for Spanish translation for the City Council meetings.  

Anthony Loera requested that the City establishes rent control. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez

6.. Revisions to the Personnel Classification and Compensation Plan by Amending the Media Specialist Classifications

2.. Approval of Minutes

4.. Fund Trade Agreement for the Exchange of Proposition A Funds With the City of Diamond Bar

1.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 1A, 23A and 23B

5.. Purchase of a Security Camera Upgrade System for the Transit Maintenance Facility and Commerce 26th Street Metrolink Station

SCHEDULED MATTERS

7.. PRESENTATION/UPDATE FROM THE SHERIFF'S DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC SAFETY IN THE CITY OF COMMERCE Sergeant Duarte provided an overview of the last two weeks.

Councilmember Lainez requested that the Deputies' response times be included in the Sheriff's reports on a monthly basis.

Mayor Argumedo emphasized the need for community outreach to inform the public that some increased activity is due to the installation of Automatic License Plate Readers. This will help explain that Deputies are now more capable of responding to and stopping crime, as well as identifying stolen vehicles.


9.. Professional Services Agreement with Vivache Designs for Mural Installation for the Pathways for Hope Project  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report and the various options available.

Councilmember Lainez expressed support for Option No. 2 and asked whether Telegraph could be included in the upcoming project. He also suggested looking into a landscaping agreement with Caltrans to incorporate it into the same project.

Vice Mayor Altamirano raised concerns about using funds from the Arts in Public Places program, noting that there is a designated arts district and he would prefer the funds to remain there. He recommended using funds from Measure AA or the general fund instead.

Further discussion ensued about utilizing Measure AA funds to cover the shortfall if the council decides to proceed with Option No. 2.


8.. Approval of Capital Improvement Program for FY 2024/2025  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Ivan Altamirano Deputy Director of Public Works Nila provided an overview of the completed, in-progress, and future requested CIP projects presented for approval.

Councilmember Lainez inquired about the lighted monument, noting that the City Council had requested specific changes. He asked when they would see the rendering of the monument for approval. City Manager Hernandez responded that the final approval would come back to them, and that currently, only the funding is being approved. Deputy Director Nila added that they have made some changes based on feedback and vetted these with Caltrans. Once the Council reviews the changes, they will present them to Caltrans for formal approval.

In response to Councilmember Garcia's query about bridge repairs, Acting Director Nila explained that some bridges have shared ownership. At Rio Hondo, a fire caused by homeless individuals necessitated repairs, and all jurisdictions involved will be contributing funding based on their share.

There was a discussion about the Bandini Library and its completion date. Acting Director Nila stated it would be completed by the end of this calendar year.

In response to a question about separate funding for potholes, Acting Director Nila explained that the repavement budget does not include repairs, hence the need for a separate funding allocation.

PUBLIC HEARING

10.. Confirmation of 2023-2024 Weed Abatement Charges  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez Director of Administrative Services and City Clerk Shumway made a brief presentation.  Mayor Argumedo opened Public Hearing.  Mayor Argumedo closed Public Hearing.  

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia reported attending the Grand Opening of the patio at the Library, the South Coast Air Quality Management District event, and the Dance Team performance. Councilmember Garcia also thanked Anthony Argular for taking photos at most of the events.

Councilmember Lainez reported attending the South Coast Air Quality Management District event and the Library Patio Grand Opening. He congratulated the water polo teams participating in the Junior Olympics for their efforts and for representing the City of Commerce. He also congratulated the Commerce Aces and wished them good luck in their San Diego tournament. Additionally, he invited everyone to National Night Out.

Vice Mayor Altamirano reported that he attended the South Coast AQMD event and reminded residents that the South Coast AQMD is offering free air filters to residents of certain areas in Commerce, encouraging them to take advantage of the program. He also attended the Garden Reading patio grand opening.

Mayor Argumedo reported attending the South Coast AQMD event, the Grand Opening at the Library, and the ICA conference in San Diego.



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 7:28 p.m. in memory of Ruben Rendon.

Meeting facilities are accessible to persons with disabilities. ln compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, notify the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 722-4805 at least 24 hours prior to the meeting.
